My first attempt at painting with watercolours. Not too shabby considering.

2026 3.title: Ariccia Sunset (Copy)
text: On today's episode of butchering artwork, we're subjecting J.M.W. Turner's Ariccia Sunset to a terrible fate.

No, of course I had no expectations going in that I'd be able to match Turner's artwork. This is my first copy of a painting, and it was an interesting experience especially considering I don't really know what I'm doing.
Unlike, say, digital or pencil (where you can undo or erase mistakes), watercolour is much more unforgiving, so any mistake I make is terribly obvious.
Also, yes, I copied an oil painting with watercolours, I'm aware.
I think the sky turned out pretty well though.
This was done using actual watercolour paper: A5, cold-pressed, medium coarse grain specifically.

2026 4.title: Venice by Moonlight, with Boats off a Campanile (Copy)
text: Yep, Turner again.
This time, I chose to actally copy a watercolour painting and one with a distinctly more 'wet' look.
That big brown splotch to the centre-left is tragic and the sky is a bit too dull, but overall it's OK enough, I think.
However, I didn't really think my choice of canvas through... I used half a page of scrap A5 print paper.
Unlike my other watercolours thus far, this was only paint, no pencil sketches done beforehand.

2026 5.title: View Over a Hilly Country, With a Stormy Sky (Copy)
text: John Constable's watercolour (sketches) were very different to Turner's, so I wanted to give one a go.
This was also done on half a page of A5 print paper. I really struggled with getting the dark colours of the original, as you can probably tell.
I also used a pencil to mimic the graphite sticks Constable used, as well as just to add some extra texture and darkness.

2026 6.title: Legendary Deirdre (Copy)
text: (1/4) This is a copy of Legendary Deirdre by Haimura Kiyotaka, originally done for Fire Emblem Heroes (FEH).
I started this on May 27, and I finished it on the 29th. Admittedly, I chose a very difficult first subject to try to copy & paint. Given that though, I'm really happy with how it turned out.
Ordinarily, this is the type of art I'd do digitally, but with my pen tablet broken, physical it is!
In the original artwork, the purples used are much more vibrant, which was very hard to replicate with the palette I was working with.
This was done on A5 watercolour paper, with pencil, pen, and watercolours (what a surprise!)
Anyway, this is one of my favourite artworks in FEH, which is why I wanted to paint it.
(2/4) These are progress pics. I forgot to take a photo of the state before this one, but it was just a rough sketch of a body frame.
(3/4) Honestly, even just sketching this dress was so troublesome.
(4/4) This is the sketch finalised before any paint was applied.
I was tempted to leave it as is because I was sure I'd ruin it with paint, but I decided to go ahead with it anyway.
Can't be afraid to ruin things if I wanna learn, after all.

2026 13.title: Lighthouse near Beachy Head
text: There was a British painter called Eric Ravillious whose exhibition I visited briefly before walking around the South Downs (and Beachy Head).
One of his paintings is of this very lighthouse, so as I was walking, I noticed it immediately. This painting was neither based on nor inspired by his work, but it's something I think about.

2026 14.title: Skyline of a London sunset
text: I really wasn't sure how to capture the colours of the buildings in the distance and settled on this weird purple, which as soon as I placed it on the paper, I realised how strange it looked. Still, bit too late for regrets, so I just completed the rest of it with that colour.
Besides the purple, I was quite pleased with how the colours turned out.
Another thing I struggled with: one side of a skyscraper was glowing orange, but I seriously could not figure out how to achieve that glowing effect.
